The live version feels more natural to me. As I type "fluffy" the list narrows on its own and the count updates right alongside it — I don't have to stop and press a button to find out if I got it right. The submit version worked too, but making me click "Search" every time is an extra step I'd rather not take. So let's go with the one that filters as I type.

I'm glad it found the potato one from a word buried in its description — that's important to me, because I don't always remember the exact title, I just remember something the page was about. Searching across the title, description, site name, and the address all sounds right. Six samples is fine for trying it out, and having the search box sit right above the collection makes sense.

One small thing I want to be sure of, since it matters to how I actually type: it shouldn't care about capital letters. If I typed "Fluffy" with a big F, I'd still expect to get the same result. Can you confirm it works that way?

Otherwise this feels good.
